summary: Intro discovery for private onramp. Customer runs inference for a conversational product with EU data residency constraints and plans to ingest PII. Primary concerns: VPC peering vs private endpoints, transit gateway routing, egress/ip gating, KMS/HSM integration, and SLA for dedicated throughput. Agreed next steps include sending network template, scheduling deep technical dive, and sharing security/compliance pack.
topics: current infra: AWS Transit Gateway + on-prem DC
egress IPs, NAT, and firewall rules
latency vs cost tradeoffs (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
timeline and success criteria for pilot
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-24 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Morgan Li (CTO), Samir Patel (Head of Security), Jamie Ortiz (Network Eng), Rosa Kim (Product)

00:00:03 Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm alex from redwood, this is priya. quick round robin?
00:00:12 Morgan: hi i'm morgan, cto at twilight shore, we build the convo product for finance customers mostly in EU.
00:00:18 Samir: samir, security. we'll be assessing data flow and key mgmt.
00:00:22 Jamie: jamie, nets. i'll be deep on peering/egress.
00:00:26 Rosa: rosa, product - focusing on latency SLAs and rollout.

00:01:05 Priya: great, thanks. objective for today is to understand your network topology, residency constraints, and what success looks like. we'll cover private onramp options: redwood dedicated vs private (vpc/privatelink) and what changes you need.

00:02:30 Morgan: high level — we have core services in eu-west-1, traffic from web frontend to our inference goes through transit gateway into a GPU cluster (self managed today) but we want to move inference to redwood private because we can't maintain ops cost. the kicker is we process some p ii and financial attributes, so data residency and auditability matter.

00:03:10 Alex: understood. do you have a timeline or pilot size?
00:03:17 Morgan: pilot first quarter — 100 qps average, spikes to 400 for short windows. want sub 150ms p95 end-to-end if possible.

00:03:45 Priya: that's helpful. two quick clarifying q's: what's your current egress pattern for third-party calls, and do you already use KMS/HSM for keys?
00:04:00 Jamie: we NAT through a pair of egress appliances, static IPs we can whitelist. transit gateway attaches our prod vpcs and a few on-prem links. for keys we use cloud-kms but legal is asking about HSM-backed keys for certain datasets.
00:04:22 Samir: yep legal will require HSM for tokens at rest for EU regulated customers. also want detailed audit logs and ability to rotate keys without service disruption.

00:05:05 Alex: ok, good. so the typical approaches are: 1) Private deployment with private endpoints (privatelink-style) where redwood instances sit in your VPC or peer via a direct private link; 2) VPC peering / TGW attachment where we connect the redwood subnets into your transit topology; 3) Dedicated hosted with IP allowlist if policy allows. each has tradeoffs re routing, egress control, and latency.

00:05:48 Rosa: can you unpack the difference practically? we care about maintenance burden and who owns the endpoint.

00:06:10 Priya: sure. privatelink/private endpoints -> we push an endpoint service and the traffic is NATted to our infra but flows over a PrivateLink connection; you keep egress control and we don't need to share route tables. VPC peering/TGW attachment -> our nodes become routable in your VPC topology, lower hop count potentially lower latency, but you need IP planning and route table updates.

00:06:55 Jamie: hm route table churn is the problem. we have hundreds of CIDR blocks for microvpcs; peering every new subnet is extra ops. private endpoints sounds cleaner but how about throughput?
00:07:10 Priya: PrivateLink bandwidth per endpoint is usually fine for our workloads; we also support load balanced endpoints and multi-az endpoints to scale. there are per-connection limits in cloud providers we'll size for your 400 spike.

00:07:40 Morgan: and latency? we measured our in-house model at ~90ms avg, 120ms p95. moving out to hosted often adds 60-80ms. we need to make sure we stay below 150ms.

00:08:00 Alex: two levers: choose peering/TGW for fewer network hops and colocate in same region, or use private endpoints but place nodes in a nearby region. also quantization and model choices affect inference time — priya can touch on that.

00:08:25 Priya: yep — for example, running on dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 with our private deployment gives you the best latency predictability. if cost is a concern we can also run a mixed strategy: prefix caching and local KV caches to mask cold-starts, plus fallback to cheaper variants for non-critical routes.

00:09:05 Samir: legal wants all data for EU customers to never leave eu-west-1. is redwood private able to spin up fully inside our region and our VPC?
00:09:18 Priya: yes — our private deployment supports VPC-only deployment inside a single region. we can deploy redwood nodes into customer-managed VPC subnets. you'll maintain the VPC, and we install agents that communicate to a control plane — note, customers can opt for private control plane for strict isolation.

00:09:42 Samir: private control plane meaning we host the control plane ourselves?
00:09:47 Alex: optional — for highest isolation we provide an on-prem or VPC-hosted control plane; it's an additional ent. option. most customers use a customer-managed control plane for Private deployments with KMS integration.

00:10:15 Jamie: about KMS — how deep is the integration? can we use our HSM? we can't hand keys to external services.
00:10:25 Priya: we support KMS + BYOK + HSM-backed keys via both AWS CloudHSM and external HSM through KMIP connectors. The private deployment nodes can be configured to call your KMS endpoints for envelope key operations so raw keys never leave your boundary. auditing is captured with our enhanced audit logs.

00:11:03 Samir: good. audit logs — can they be shipped to our SIEM? we want CloudTrail-like events for each inference request (at least metadata, not payload).
00:11:15 Alex: yes, we stream audit events to customer S3 or SIEM via Kinesis/CloudWatch or syslog. we redact payloads by default but you can opt-in to additional fields. we'll share the schema.

00:11:40 Morgan: earlier you said private control plane is an add-on. what are the networking differences between private control plane vs shared control plane?
00:11:52 Priya: with shared control plane you run data plane in your VPC and our control calls home over a secure channel; with private control plane the control plane endpoints are in your VPC as well, so you can restrict all traffic internally. which is what you want for full air-gapped-style compliance.

00:12:20 Jamie: ok what about egress — our firewall team insists on static egress IPs and we need to keep egress inside EU. how does redwood handle egress for updates, image pulls, patches?
00:12:32 Alex: for private deployments we can route all egress through your NAT/egress appliances; image pulls can be from your internal registry or proxied through your egress. if you prefer, we also have an option to supply images pushed into your registry as part of setup.

00:12:56 Rosa: timeline question — pilot in q1, who's the primary contact from redwood to manage the onboarding?
00:13:04 Alex: i'll own the commercial side, priya is SE lead for the technical onboarding. we'll put a project manager on once the pilot is greenlit.

00:13:30 Jamie: couple nitty gritty — IP planning. if we do TGW attachment we need to reserve /24s or /23s per AZ? what's recommended?
00:13:42 Priya: we typically recommend at least /24 per AZ for node pools to avoid IP exhaustion; for high scale you might want /23. we'll share an IP planning template.

00:14:05 Morgan: what about routing asymmetry? our security devices expect symmetric flows. peering might change source nat behavior.

00:14:16 Priya: fair — we can support both source and destination nat configurations. if you need symmetric flows we can configure SNAT on the redwood nodes or leverage egress through your NAT gateway so the flow stays consistent.

00:14:45 Samir: encryption in flight — TLS termination where? we can't have plaintext inside the VPC.
00:14:51 Alex: TLS is terminated at the node with mutual TLS to control plane; within customer VPC we can use TLS between app and the private endpoint. nothing is in plaintext by default.

00:15:25 Morgan: ok i'm worried about perf — do you have reference benchmarks for eu-west-1 private deployment?
00:15:33 Priya: we have public perf sheets for standard models and a private benchmark template we run for customers; i'll add a note to run a small perf test during the pilot. note that quantized variants and kernel selection affect latency heavily.

00:16:10 Jamie: one more — peering with on-prem through TGW: we have existing IP overlaps for some satellite offices. do you support NATing at the attachment?
00:16:24 Priya: yes, we support SNAT on a per-attachment basis to avoid overlaps. it's part of the onboarding checklist.

00:16:55 Morgan: legal will ask about indemnity and data processing addendum. do you have a standard DPA?
00:17:03 Alex: yes, we have a DPA and EU SCC options. i'll include a copy.

00:17:20 Rosa: pricing — rough T-shirt estimates? we need to budget for pilot but also for steady state.
00:17:29 Alex: for private deployment there's a platform fee plus per-inference token costs; dedicated reserved capacity is an upfront commit that reduces per-token cost and gives predictable throughput. i'll include a dedicated vs private cost example for your expected qps.

00:17:55 Samir: competitor question — we evaluated BigCloud AI but they didn't have strong private control plane. any notable differences we should expect?
00:18:07 Priya: compared to large cloud offerings, our differentiation is production-grade inference tooling (prefix caching, KV cache, rollouts) and the ability to run the same runtime across hosted/dedicated/private with observability hooks.

00:18:40 Jamie: operationally how do we patch nodes? do you orchestrate upgrades or we do?
00:18:49 Priya: we coordinate. for private deployments we can either hand you OCI images and patching scripts or manage the lifecycle on agreed maintenance windows.

00:19:10 Morgan: any outage isolation? like if a node misbehaves, can it be drained without impacting traffic?
00:19:18 Priya: yes we have graceful draining, automatic fallback to healthy nodes, and can route to a fallback model variant if capacity dips. that's part of our reliability guarantees.

00:19:45 Samir: compliance — can we get a SOC2 report and pen test summary?
00:19:52 Alex: yes, will attach both. we also provide an architecture compliance pack showing network flows and hardening steps. link: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack (note: placeholder)

00:20:25 Rosa: for success criteria, list them: 1) sub-150ms p95 in eu-west-1, 2) auditability to SIEM, 3) HSM-backed key ops, 4) no data leaving eu region.
00:20:40 Alex: sounds right. we'll map those to pilot acceptance criteria.

00:21:05 Priya: quick question on feature gating — will you need function/tool-calling or just plain text generation and embeddings?
00:21:14 Morgan: initially chat generation + embeddings for semantic search. function calling later.

00:21:40 Jamie: what about peering cost? if we attach to TGW we pay for bytes. is that on us?
00:21:47 Alex: generally cross-account bandwidth costs are billed by the cloud provider and would be on your side; we can work with you to estimate egress. for dedicated capacity hosted by redwood we include internal networking in the commitment.

00:22:20 Samir: data residency enforcement mechanism — how do we enforce region restriction for models?
00:22:29 Priya: policy layer: you can pin model versions to region, and routing policies prevent forwarding to non-compliant regions. we also implement blocklists at control plane for certain tenant metadata.

00:23:05 Morgan: ok that helps. let's talk about the pilot scope — minimal footprint to validate latency and audibility: 2 AZ nodes, private endpoints into our prod vpc, run 2k requests for perf test over 24 hours.
00:23:18 Priya: good, we'll propose a pilot plan in the follow-up email.

00:24:00 Alex: any blockers on your side to get started?
00:24:05 Jamie: need approval from infra for opening endpoint connection, and legal sign-off on DPA.
00:24:12 Samir: also need assurance that payloads are redacted in logs by default; we don't want raw p ii persisted.
00:24:20 Priya: default is redact PII; we'll include the redaction policy and retention windows.

00:25:00 Morgan: ok let's capture the explicit network asks: we'll share TGW attachments, routing tables, NAT egress IPs, and a list of overlapping CIDRs.

00:25:18 Alex: perfect. we'll send the IP plan template and sample IP allocations.

00:25:46 (small crosstalk)
00:26:10 Priya: i'll also call out options for multi-region standby in case you need DR outside eu-west-1 but still within EU region constraints — e.g., eu-west-3 as standby.

00:26:40 Rosa: would that violate residency? standby needs to be eu as well for these customers.
00:26:45 Priya: yep keep DR inside EU — we won't route outside EU for EU-restricted tenants.

00:27:10 Jamie: one more question — are there specific port requirements for the data plane?
00:27:18 Priya: we'll provide a short port list: 443 for control plane TLS, 8200 for internal health probes (can be tunneled), and ephemeral ports for node-to-node. full list in template.

00:27:55 Samir: firewall team often wants to see cert pinning. can you support mTLS?
00:28:03 Alex: yes mTLS available between your services and our endpoints; cert rotation integrated with KMS where relevant.

00:28:35 Morgan: ok i think we have enough to proceed to next step.

00:28:58 Alex: recap — action items: we'll send network template, security pack, DPA, SOC2, and schedule a deep dive next week. Priya will prepare perf/cost slides.

00:29:20 Jamie: timeline, again — target pilot kickoff first week of Jan, but we'd like to start prep now.

00:29:33 Alex: totally. we'll line up the technical call. priya — you OK for 31st?
00:29:39 Priya: yep i'll block time.

00:30:05 Rosa: any blockers re contract? we need price ballpark to get legal engaged.
00:30:12 Alex: i'll send a ballpark cost sheet in the follow-up. nothing final until we scope the pilot.

00:30:35 (brief pause)
00:31:00 Samir: quick question about observability — does redwood provide per-request tracing headers we can ingest?
00:31:08 Priya: yes we emit trace IDs and can forward spans to your tracing backend. we'll share the trace schema.

00:31:45 Morgan: do you support structured output and function calling soon? planned?
00:31:52 Priya: function calling is supported in hosted now and will be supported in private deployments in the onboarding window — we can enable it for pilot if needed.

00:32:18 Alex: ok final recap and next steps. again: deliverables from redwood: security-pack + SOC2 + DPA, network-template.xlsx, ip recommendations, perf/cost slide deck. deliverables from twilight shore: TGW attachments, routing tables, egress static IPs, list of overlapping CIDRs. schedule follow-up tech deep dive.

00:33:00 Morgan: good. thanks all.
00:33:05 Alex: thanks, we'll send follow-up with links.
00:33:12 (meeting winds down, many say thanks)

00:34:00 Post-meeting note: Alex mentions link to security docs in chat: <link:security-pack.pdf> and IP template: <link:network-template.xlsx>.

00:35:00 Closing remarks: all agreed to follow-up timeline.

(Transcript ends - remainder of time used for quick side sync between Alex and Priya about internal next steps)
